First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
p^2 + 27 & = 0\[3pt]

p^2 & = -27 
}
$$

By taking the square root, we obtain

$$
p = \pm \sqrt{-27}.
$$

We now rewrite $p$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =\pm \sqrt{-27} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{27\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{27}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{{3}^{2}\cdot 3}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm 3\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm 3\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p = \pm 3\sqrt{3} \, \textrm{i}.$
